items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: So we come in, Harry Leroy and Mitzi Mayfair already did their dance... I said to Harry Leroy, 'How's it going, Harry?'

ctx.x: sold me, neither one. The man who is going to hire me is going to pay me more money than what he said and more money than what Nazarro said. See what I mean? So I got past that one and Nazarro turned around to Mr. Ziegfeld, God rest his soul, turned around and said, Gene Buck, give them a contract. Just like that. Give us a contract.

We go in this show, man, and never look back. Never look back. It was the greatest show that we ever had in life. Greatest showtime, because we did the shows and the shows were so pleasing that we stood out like a sore thumb, you know. We were the only ones that had vagabond clothes on in the show. We were the only ones that had dancing of the style that we were doing it, 'cause Mitzi Mayfair was a dancer and so was Harry Leroy, but they were a different style. I had the down-to-earth style, you see and they…

our act, they'd change our act. They'd change the position of our act on every show until finally they got us down to where we could only go on next to closing and after us came the finale. Harry Richman singing the finale. "Get the beat, of people's feet, walking up and down the street, Going to New York" That was the finale of the show and after we did our number, did our song and all, next comes on the finale. In other words, while we were doing -- we rehearsed about five hours over at Nazarro's hotel to get…
